The Crow Tribe adopted by resolution on January 31, 1976, a Crow Tribal Law and Order Code, which allegedly assumes all civil and criminal jurisdiction within the Crow Reservation boundaries. The implications of this action await assessment, but if put into total action would have far reaching effects on the residents of the reservation as well as on inter-racial and inter-governmental relations. Other jurisdictional issues include a Land Use Zoning Ordinance, Environmental Health and Sanitation Ordinance and a ordinance for the taxation of all coal produced on the reservation and Ceded Area. These ordinances also were adopted by the Crow Tribal Council on January 31, 1976, and are discussed in more detail later in this chapter.
Attitudes Toward Development
The most comprehensive study of knowledge and attitudes of the Crow Indians concerning coal development is a survey conducted by the Crow Tribe's Office of Coal Research in 1975. A condensed report of this survey was published in the Hardin Herald. The complete survey is available through the Crow Tribes Office of Coal Research, Crow Agency, Montana.
The most apparent conclusions drawn from this survey were that the Crow population is greatly deficient in knowledge about coal related development, and that Tribal members are about evenly split as to favoring or not favoring coal development. The Office of Coal Research is presently training interviewers to conduct another survey concerning Crow coal development.
